How an order runs

From brief to boxed.

Every order follows the same five steps. Nothing goes to production without an approved sample.

  1. Brief

    Garment, quantity, technique, date and your artwork.

  2. Proposal

    Recommended garment and technique, with price per volume.

  3. Sample

    A physical pre-production sample with your real artwork.

  4. Production

    Scheduled on the press that fits your run and colors.

  5. Delivery

    Inspected, folded and packed. Shipping across Mexico and abroad.

Cutting

Precision cutting of knit and woven fabrics.

Sewing

Made-to-measure garments, from fabric to final seam.

Embroidery

Flat, 3D embroidery and patches.

Dye & wash

Stone and enzyme washes, custom colors.

Since 1990 · Puebla

35 years on the press.

It started with a hand-built table and logos on t-shirts. Today it is an audited plant printing for global licenses.

1º
First place · Textile · PNAG 2025 Premio Nacional de Artes Gráficas 2025, textile category, with the project “Einstein: Abre tu mente”.
Read the note ↗
  1. 1990

    Estampados Especiales

    Federico Chilian starts printing logos on t-shirts in Puebla. His first screen printing table was built with hinges bought with 6 pesos from his father.

  2. Group

    From a workshop to Grupo Chilian

    Estampados Especiales, Promocionales Especiales, FDE Industries and Sport Exalta: printing, promotional items and sportswear under one group.

  3. Plant

    Santa Isabel Cholula

    Eight Roq and M&R automatic presses, cutting, sewing, embroidery and dyeing: up to 20,000 pieces a day. The showroom lives inside the plant.

  4. Industry

    A voice for the apparel sector

    Federico Chilian presided over the apparel industry chamber (CANAIVE) Puebla–Tlaxcala and speaks at Canagraf Puebla events on custom production.

  5. 2025

    National Graphic Arts Award

    First place in the textile category with “Einstein: Abre tu mente”, a print recognized for its technique, quality and complexity.

  6. 2026

    SMETA, Walmart, C&A and FAMA

    Social compliance approvals renewed: labor standards, health and safety, environment and business ethics.

Questions brands ask

Before you place a program.

Audits, capacity, minimums, sampling and logistics, answered.

Which brands and licenses have you produced for?

Our plant has printed brands and licenses such as Carhartt, The North Face, Vans, Supreme, Marvel, Bluey, Minecraft, Snoopy and Tom and Jerry.

Which audits does the plant have?

Walt Disney FAMA, WRAP, VF Corporation and C&A, with 2026 social compliance approvals from SMETA (Sedex) and Walmart, and chemical management with ChemIQ: the standards retailers such as Walmart, Amazon, Costco, Disney, Carhartt, Nike and adidas ask for.

What is your production capacity?

Up to 20,000 pieces a day, with 8 automatic Roq and M&R presses, 2 DTG printers, a 6-head embroidery machine, and cutting, sewing, dyeing and washing in the same plant.

Do you do full package or decoration only?

Both: we decorate your blank garments, or we cut, sew, dye and print from the fabric.

What is the minimum order for brands?

Brands and OEM from 600 pieces. For samples and short runs, DTG from 1 piece; the sublimated Chilian Sport performance tee from 6 pieces.

How does an order run?

Five steps: brief, proposal with volume pricing, a physical pre-production sample with your real artwork, production and delivery. Nothing goes into production without an approved sample.

Do you work with US brands?

Yes. A dedicated US contact takes your run from approval to delivery, with a bilingual team in the same time zones and coordinated import logistics.

Where is the plant and can we visit?

Tlacomulco No. 2, San Pablo Ahuatempan, Santa Isabel Cholula, Puebla, Mexico, ZIP 74355. The showroom is inside the plant, so you see samples and production in one visit, Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 18:00.

How do I get a quote and how fast do you reply?

“Quote in a minute” shows a reference price instantly. Send your request and your advisor replies within one business day with the final price.
